This is a mechanism-control study, not a new physical rebonding model.

static_shield_control_mechanism.implementation: arrhenius_fracture/persistent_site_coupled_hazard_v10229.py, _phase_statistics() -- a new, default-off, mutually-exclusive-with-hazard_coupled branch keyed on engine._static_shield_control (set externally by the run script, not derived from any internal engine counter). This is the CONFIRMED correct injection point for the real production engine hierarchy (CorrectedHazardEnergyGatedPersistentSiteCyclicTipEngine), per docs/v10_2_30_crack_rebonding_equation_lineage.md's 'injection-point correction history': CoupledPersistentSiteCyclicTipEngine.cycle_step_waveform bypasses persistent_site_cyclic_v10229.py's own preview_cycle_waveform/cycle_step_waveform entirely (that location is documented dead code for this engine hierarchy, exactly as it was for the original dynamic-rebonding implementation's own first two injection attempts), delegating instead to integrate_state_coupled_waveform/_phase_statistics. An initial implementation attempt was placed at the dead-code location and empirically showed ZERO waiting-time sensitivity even at K_b comparable to Kmax itself -- caught by a direct K_b sensitivity sweep before any real trajectory was run -- and corrected to this location, which shows a consistent, physically sensible ~34% waiting-time increase at K_b=900000 Pa sqrt(m) and correct saturation/censoring at more extreme K_b.
